judgements.referenceQuote: Mia Amor Mottley[1] (born 1 October 1965) is a Barbadian politician and lawyer who has served as the eighth prime minister of Barbados since 2018 and as Leader of the Barbados Labour Party (BLP) since 2008. Mottley is the first woman to hold both positions.
judgements.rationale: The dossier contains no claims at all, so the fact that Mottley became Barbados's first woman prime minister in 2018 is not stated anywhere in the supplied material.

judgements.referenceQuote: In 2018, her party won a historic landslide victory in the 24 May general election, securing all 30 seats in the House and 72.8% of the popular vote
judgements.rationale: The dossier is empty; no claim describes the May 2018 general election result (all 30 House seats, 72.8% of the popular vote), so the fact cannot be recovered.

judgements.referenceQuote: Mottley first entered Barbadian politics in 1991, when she lost an election race in St. Michael North East against Leroy Brathwaite (a defeat of fewer than 200 votes).

usefulness.rationale: The dossier contains no content at all: person name, identity anchors, and confusable-with list aside, there are no passages and no retained sources. A reader learns only two anchor facts (Barbadian politician/lawyer, MP for Saint Michael North East, PM from 2018) and cannot learn what she actually did, prepare for a conversation, or verify any claims. There are no dossier statements to assess for overclaims, so no findings can be reported; the two listed unjustified conclusions reference sources that are not provided, so they cannot be matched to any citation. Scores are zero by absence of evidence, not by contradiction.
